day_shape: 77 items: US launches 'Operation Economic Outcast' with State/OFAC sanctions on Iran's military, cyber and oil networks, CENTCOM reports 71 vessels redirected under Iran blockade, Syria formally delisted as state sponsor of terrorism, Pakistan army chief Munir visits Tehran on Hormuz de-escalation, Netanyahu claims Iran tried to assassinate his son; nothing from UK Parliament or IAEA.

threads.label: Operation Economic Outcast sanctions rollout
threads.summary: The US State Department and OFAC announced 'Operation Economic Outcast', sanctioning entities, individuals and vessels tied to Iran's military procurement, cyber intrusions and illicit petroleum trade. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the campaign, Defense Secretary Hegseth said military force remained on the table, and Trump posted that Iran was 'completely collapsing'.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and naval blockade
threads.summary: CENTCOM said forces aboard USS George H.W. Bush had redirected 71 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two enforcing the US blockade on Iran, with more than 40 aid vessels allowed through. Iran warned vessels violating its Hormuz transit rules could face fines or seizure, an Iranian parliamentary committee advanced a plan to charge vessels for services, and Rubio reiterated to Germany's Wadephul a shared commitment to freedom of navigation.

threads.label: Pakistan army chief Munir visits Tehran
threads.summary: Pakistan army chief Asim Munir held talks in Tehran that the Pakistan army called 'constructive', with the Jerusalem Post reporting discussions focused on preventing further escalation and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Munir had earlier spoken with President Trump, according to three Pakistani sources cited by JPost, and Defa Press ran commentary linking his enhanced authority to Pakistan's new defence law.

threads.label: Syria delisted as terrorism sponsor
threads.summary: Secretary Rubio authorised the formal rescission of Syria's designation as a State Sponsor of Terrorism after the 45-day Congressional notification period, and also delisted Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist. Defa Press reported the decision took effect after Congress's review period ended Friday without action.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes and West Bank operations
threads.summary: The IDF said it destroyed two Hamas weapons depots inside mosques in Gaza City and Deir al-Balah, struck two Hamas operatives who took part in the 7 October 2023 attack including Nukhba member Mohammad Abd al-Nasser Jabr Abu Asaad, and apprehended Imam Khazzam in Jenin. IRIB reported artillery fire on north Al-Bureij camp and simultaneous raids across West Bank provinces including Jenin, Ramallah and Hebron.

threads.label: Iran domestic strains and threat rhetoric
threads.summary: Iran International reported fuel shortages closing Tehran petrol stations, a debate over Mohsen Rezaei's threats to halt oil exports, and an Instagram poll of about 100,000 respondents in which 9 in 10 rejected marriage or children under current conditions. JPost cited an Iranian Channel 3 video threatening Barron Trump with a $10m bounty, PM Netanyahu's claim Iran tried to assassinate one of his sons, and a UK briefing to energy chiefs after Iran-linked hackers shut a small facility.

threads.label: Regime channel messaging on wars and resistance
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a message from Mojtaba Khamenei describing an 'unprecedented funeral procession' in Iraq as demonstrating Iran-Iraq solidarity, while IRIB carried police chief Radan pledging readiness against 'unrest' and quoted Guterres saying war with Iran showed the limits of superpower strength. Defa Press ran commentary on 'the second and third imposed wars', Ansarullah's capabilities against Saudi Arabia, and claims that petrol prices rose in 145 countries since the war began.

events.source_detail: Times of Israel · military correspondent · X (via rss.app)
events.title: The Israeli military says it destroyed two Hamas weapon depots in the Gaza Strip which were located inside mosques. The mosques in Gaza City and Deir al-Balah were used by Hamas to store dozens of assault rifles and other weapons, according to the IDF. "This is another example of Hamas’s systematic exploitation of civilian infrastructure, including mosques, in violation of international law, to advance and execute terror attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians," the military says. Ahead of the strikes, the IDF published warnings to Palestinians residing in the area.
events.summary:
